evidence.label: API
evidence.description: The check reads the server's result through the editor's API or its LSP client: requests, providers, published diagnostics, and the extension's output channel.

evidence.label: UI state
evidence.description: The check drives the editor through its keys and reads the state of its UI: windows and their text, menus and their items, mappings, the mode, and message histories. It doesn't see how they look.

evidence.label: process
evidence.description: The check observes processes: exit statuses, deadlines, process groups, and what is left running.

evidence.label: configuration
evidence.description: The check verifies the test's own inputs and setup: prerequisites, pinned versions, installations, key mappings, and the evidence it keeps.

evidence.label: manual
evidence.description: A person observed it. Manual records are optional: the release gate never requires one.

conditions.description: The extension is installed from a VSIX: run.cjs with --vsix, and every Remote-SSH launch. Without it, run.cjs loads the extension from source, and the check doesn't run.
The client declares workspace.didChangeWatchedFiles.dynamicRegistration, as Neovim does on macOS, so the server registers file watchers.
The client doesn't declare file watching, as Neovim on Linux doesn't; the server notices a change on disk at the next .v3 change.

checks.description: The client initializes on bad.v3, with the root directory of the fixture's .virgil-lsp.json and the server's name, virgil-lsp.
bad.v3 has exactly one diagnostic, the parser's "invalid start of expression" from aeneas, an error at line 3, column 27.
bad.v3, which doesn't parse, has no document symbols.
An unsaved edit that fixes bad.v3 publishes, for a newer version, no diagnostics, and vim.diagnostic has none.
After the edit, document symbols are the component C and the variant V, with its case A as its child, selecting A's name.
The configuration passes VIRGIL_LOC as initializationOptions.virgilRoot, and the project file has no diagnostics.
words/Words.v3 has exactly one diagnostic, the TypeError "expected int in var initialization, got Array<byte>"; its line and severity aren't checked.
A definition request on StringBuilder returns the name of class StringBuilder in lib/util/StringBuilder.v3.
A hover request there returns class StringBuilder in a virgil code block, with the use's range.
Signature help just after the ( of .puts(a) returns def puts(s: Array<byte>) -> this, with its parameter active, at label offsets 9 to 23.
A workspace symbol request for join returns first the method join in words/Words.v3, with its range.
References of StringBuilder, with its declaration, are the use, the class's name, and uses in other lib/util files, each spelling the name, sorted, without repeats.
Document highlights of StringBuilder are exactly its use in words/Words.v3, with kind Text and no other file's ranges.
After an unsaved fix, vim.lsp.buf.rename renames both uses of the local line to text; one undo restores them, and another restores the type error's text.
Completion after an unsaved whi offers the keyword while, whose edit replaces the prefix; applying it gives while, and undo restores the line.
Completion after li ranks line, a, b, this, and join first; line is a Variable with the detail var line: int and sortText 0000; applying it and undo restore the line.
Completion after a., with the trigger character ., returns only length, a Field with the detail def length: int; applying it and undo restore the line.
The client attaches to .virgil-lsp.json, and no client attaches to package.json.
An unsaved "bogus": 1 in .virgil-lsp.json gives an UnknownField diagnostic, which clears when the line is removed.
Stopping the client makes the server exit with code 0 and signal 0, and the client is removed.
Neovim 0.11 or later is on PATH, and the server and its worker are executable; without Neovim the test is skipped unless REQUIRE_NVIM=1.
Headless Neovim exits with status 0 within the 120-second deadline.
A UI is attached, UIEnter and LazyVim's VeryLazy fired, and noice.nvim is loaded.
The client initializes on bad.v3 with the fixture's root directory, the server's name, the command virgil-lsp --stdio, and VIRGIL_LOC as virgilRoot.
bad.v3 has exactly one diagnostic, the parser's error at line 3, column 27, and no document symbols.
An unsaved edit clears the diagnostic for a newer version; undo restores the text and the parser diagnostic; redo reapplies the edit.
After the edit, document symbols are C and V, with its case A as its child, selecting A's name.
The project file, with lib/util from VIRGIL_LOC, has no diagnostics.
words/Words.v3, attached to the project's client, has exactly one diagnostic, the expected TypeError.
Document symbols of words/Words.v3 are the component Words with its method join.
A definition request on StringBuilder returns the name of class StringBuilder in lib/util/StringBuilder.v3.
LazyVim's buffer mapping gd, pressed on StringBuilder, opens lib/util/StringBuilder.v3 at the class, which gets a client of its own.
A hover request there returns class StringBuilder in a virgil code block, with the use's range.
K opens a floating window whose text has class StringBuilder, and it closes when the cursor moves.
Signature help just after the ( of .puts(a) returns def puts with its parameter at label offsets 9 to 23, and nothing just past the ).
A workspace symbol request for join returns first the method join in words/Words.v3, with its range.
References of StringBuilder are the use, the class's name, and uses in other lib/util files, each spelling the name, sorted, without repeats.
While the type error stands, <leader>cr shows the server's reason in noice's message history, opens no prompt, and changes nothing.
After an unsaved fix clears the diagnostics, <leader>cr's prompt offers line; entering text renames both uses; one u restores them, a second the TypeError.
Typing ( after .puts makes noice request signature help and show def puts in a window; a request at the cursor returns it with its parameter active.
Restoring words/Words.v3's text publishes the TypeError alone again.
In Insert mode, <C-k> from a closed window sends a request answered with def puts and shows it in a window.
Insert mode's <C-s> is LazyVim's Save File, not signature help; the test doesn't press it.
In Normal mode, gK sends a request answered with def puts and shows it in a window.
Typing w shows blink.cmp's menu with the server's keyword while; after whi the menu starts with while and lacks return; Enter gives while, and undo restores the file.
Typing li shows a menu that starts with the server's line, a Variable with var line: int; Enter gives line, and undo restores the file.
Typing a. makes blink.cmp ask with the trigger character ., and the server's only item is length, a Field with def length: int; Enter gives a.length, and undo restores the file.
In the comment, after a word and after ., the menu has no item from the server, and every request seen there was answered with none; zero requests also pass.
In Ints.max(1, with no ), typing , shows max with b: int highlighted, a request at the cursor has the second parameter active, and <C-k> shows it again.
In Ints.max(1, ) that mini.pairs closed, typing , shows max with b: int highlighted, and a request at the cursor has the second parameter active.
With the project file never opened, "bogus": 1 written on disk gives UnknownField without a .v3 change; restoring the file clears it, and the TypeError returns.
"bogus": 1 written on disk gives no UnknownField within 3 seconds, and gives it after the next .v3 change; restoring the file clears it, and the TypeError returns.
The client attaches to .virgil-lsp.json and not to package.json; an unsaved "bogus": 1 gives UnknownField on its line, and undo clears it.
A bare :lsp restart replaces only the current buffer's clients, which exit with code 0 and signal 0 or 15; the new client reattaches and republishes the TypeError; others keep running.
A bare :LspRestart replaces every client, each exiting with code 0 and signal 0 or 15; the new client reattaches and republishes the TypeError.
A restart naming virgil_lsp, with :lsp restart or :LspRestart as the Neovim version has, replaces the clients, each exiting with code 0 and signal 0, and the new client republishes the TypeError.
Stopping every client makes each server exit with code 0 and signal 0, and the clients are removed.
With VIRGIL_LOC unset and a deliberately bundle-less server, a client initializes on .virgil-lsp.json.
The project file gets a MissingVirgilRoot diagnostic on its virgilDependencies line, which vim.diagnostic has too.
noice.nvim's message history has the server's Invalid project file warning within 5 seconds; in the stock profile the noice-1074-7bfd942 rule expects it to fail.
Stopping the client makes the server exit with code 0 and signal 0.
The arguments, the archive or the server with its worker, an empty output directory, nvim, tmux, git, and python3, Neovim 0.11 or later, and the pinned Virgil sources.

words/Words.v3 has exactly one diagnostic, the TypeError from aeneas with its message, on line 7.

The reference provider returns the use, the class's name, and uses in other lib/util files, each spelling StringBuilder.

The test kills the server with SIGKILL, then runs Virgil: Restart Language Server while the recovery's start is held, and nothing stops the recovering client or starts another before the hold is released. The recovered server's input starts with initialize, then has initialized, and ends with exactly one shutdown and one exit, with exit last; it gets the open bad.v3 in a didOpen before exit, on either side of shutdown, and exits with status 0. The replacement starts, the type error returns, exactly one virgil-lsp is left with no worker but its own, and no request or notification fails.

The test kills the server with SIGKILL, then changes virgil.server.path back from the recovery script to the server while the recovery's start is held, and nothing stops the recovering client or starts another before the hold is released. The recovered server's input starts with initialize, then has initialized, and ends with exactly one shutdown and one exit, with exit last; it gets the open bad.v3 in a didOpen before exit, on either side of shutdown, and exits with status 0. The original server starts as the replacement, the type error returns, exactly one virgil-lsp is left with no worker but its own, and no request or notification fails.

The server runs as the child of a script that keeps the client's output open after the server exits. The test kills the server with SIGKILL, waits for its exit status, 137, and requests a hover, which the client writes to the dead server: the write fails with EPIPE, and the client logs it. The client then restarts the server exactly once, without stopping: the log says the server will restart, once, and never "Shutting down server." or that it will not be restarted, and the script records two starts. The restarted server's input starts with initialize, then has initialized and didOpens for the open bad.v3 and words/Words.v3 with the editor's text and version, and its diagnostics return. Released, the script exits, and only the restarted server's virgil-lsp is left, with no worker but its own.

The server runs as the child of a script that, once bad.v3 has its parser diagnostic and words/Words.v3 its type error, writes a line that isn't a message to the client, before the server's answer to a hover. The client logs that the connection to the server is erroring and "Shutting down server.", and stops: the diagnostics of bad.v3 and words/Words.v3 and the document symbols of bad.v3 are gone at once. The log then says that stopping the server timed out, and that the script exited, with SIGKILL or status 137, once; the script, the server, and its worker are gone, the script recorded no other start, and the log never says that the server will restart or will not be restarted.

The test kills the server with SIGKILL 5 times in a row, each time once the server that the client started has published bad.v3's diagnostic. The client restarts it 4 times, then logs vscode-languageclient's message that the server crashed 5 times in the last 3 minutes and will not be restarted, once; the 5 exits are logged, no other server starts, bad.v3's diagnostics are gone, and no virgil-lsp or virgil-lsp-worker is left.

The test starts the server from a script that records its input, makes an unsaved edit that replaces bad.v3 with a component RestartLatest, and at once, with no request or notification between, runs Virgil: Restart Language Server; exactly one replacement starts. The old server got bad.v3's saved text in a didOpen and no didChange with RestartLatest, which would mean that the edit wasn't pending, and exited with status 0. The replacement's didOpen has the buffer's exact text and version, and the document symbols are RestartLatest alone. A later unsaved edit, to RestartLater, reaches the replacement in a didChange with its exact text and version, and the symbols become RestartLater alone.
A supplied VSIX exists, the server and its worker are executable, and the pinned VS Code downloads.
VS Code's --install-extension installs the VSIX into the launch's empty extensions directory, exiting with status 0 within 120 seconds.
VS Code, with the suite in its Extension Host, exits with status 0 within 120 seconds, and its process group exits.
After the window closes, no virgil-lsp or virgil-lsp-worker is left in VS Code's process group within 5 seconds, and the last server exit in the log, if logged, is clean.

The third launch opens the fixture; the suite kills the server and ends while the recovery's start is held, which closes the window, and the script records exactly the killed server's start and the recovery's. Only the extension host's terminating log releases the start, and the client logged the recovery. The recovered server received initialize and initialized, the open bad.v3 in a didOpen before exit, exactly one shutdown and a final exit, and exited with status 0.

bootstrap.cjs started and passed, VS Code exited with status 0, the suite printed a PASS line and no FAIL line, and VS Code's processes didn't outlive it.
No language server is left on the host 5 seconds after the window's client exits, or after the test stops a remote extension host that VS Code left running.
The client's and the host's logs are collected before the teardown, connection tokens are removed from the copies, and summary.txt and manifest.json are written.
The teardown stops every process of the run and confirms that none is left and the SSH server's port is closed.

gapKinds.description: What the editor shows, which automation can't observe: rendered views, popups, menus, notifications, prompts, and layout. A permanent gap.
Behavior that no automated check exercises. It stays not covered until a check that exercises it is added, which planned names when one is.

xfails.label: missing-root warning
xfails.description: noice.nvim at this commit drops every server's window/showMessage, so the stock configuration never shows the Invalid project file warning. The check is expected to fail only in the noroot profile, only at this commit, only by not observing the warning, and only when the required checks pass in the same profile and iteration. Observing the warning is an XPASS, which fails. The workaround profile must pass the check normally.
